newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may let foreigners buy Petrobras vote shrs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may let foreigners buy Petrobras vote shrs.

text.p: Brazil, moving to open its oil sector to private capital, may allow foreigners to buy a minority voting stake in state oil monopoly Petrobras, a lawmaker said.

Dep. Eliseu Rezende, the Congress lower house member charged with preparing enabling legislation for Brazil's new Oil Law, told reporters his draft bill opens Petrobras' capital stock to foreign investors.
He said the draft rules, nonetheless, maintain the state's majority ownership of 50 percent plus one voting share of Petrobras.
"Petrobras will not be privatized but it will be opened (to foreign capital)," Rezende said.

He also said the draft bill he plans to present to Congress next week would replace a law that grants Petrobras its monopoly status, bans foreign voting stock ownership and limits native Brazilians to a 0.1-percent holding. He gave no time frame for a possible stock sale.
His comments confirmed a report Friday in a local
financial daily, which also said the government, if the legislation were passed, would place 30 percent of the Petrobras voting common it owns.

Preferred and common shares of Petrobras have surged since this week, partly on speculation regarding Rezende draft bill. Petrobras preferred was up 3.22 percent at 192.50 reais while its voting common was 1.38 percent at 147.00 reais at 1621 local/1321 est Friday on the Sao Paulo bourse.

Rezende, a member of the government-allied Liberal Front Party (PFL), said his draft rules also bar Petrobras from directly distributing natural gas to large consumers and create a National Petroleum Agency to regulate the oil sector. ((--James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413))
